note: Every engine FrameMotion can render. Own engines have a page (relative to this folder) that sets window.__framemotion. Bundled engines have a build (a builder in kit/builders.mjs makes their page in a temporary folder) and adapter renderFrame. sources name entries of integrations/sources.json; blocks are modules other engines may import. params declares each engine setting (type, default, min, max); width and height are always allowed and the renderer refuses anything else. optional lists files a page may ask for that are allowed to be missing (a film's music in a silent render); any other missing file fails the render. A param marked timing changes the engine's duration or frame rate, so the renderer then takes those from the page instead of the registry. group, about, good_for and inputs feed the welcome menu (scripts/engine_menu.py) and the per-scene engine choice: group names one of groups, about is one plain sentence for the user, good_for and inputs name what the engine is good for and what it takes. method_of names the engine an entry is a second way of animating (the same look by another method, Kamil 2026-11-20: duplicates improve an engine, never a second one); the menu lists it under that engine, not on its own, and the engine renders it with the setting "way": the way's id (render-engine.mjs resolveWay; "default" or no way is the engine's own film).

style.about: the style: crayon, cyanotype, paper-collage, toy-theatre, oil, woodblock, scratchboard, single-line-engraving, stipple, pixel-art, flat-vector, isometric, coloured-pencil, pencil-watercolour, risograph, ink-wash, mid-century, rubber-hose, low-poly, broken-colour, charcoal, dream-glaze, embroidery, folk-tale, halftone, scrapbook, storybook, toy-brick, sumi-e, marker-comic, chalkboard, ballpoint, motif (your own picture: set motif and medium) (or a style added to styles.json)

from.about: seconds to skip after the style's own start (the first moment with a mark, so the reel does not open on blank paper)

blank_start.about: open on the blank page (frame 0 of the film) instead of the first mark

length.about: render length in seconds: the drawing is fitted into it (faster or slower, for a 5 to 8 s reel); 0 keeps the film's own pace

brightness.about: brightness on top of the style's own (1 = as the style is set; oil is lifted for phone screens)

contrast.about: contrast on top of the style's own (1 = as the style is set; ballpoint and stipple are firmer)

motif.about: for the style "motif": the path to your SVG (a logo, an icon or line art, drawn line by line and coloured in) or PNG/JPG (revealed by hand strokes)

scene.about: a scene of your own, drawn in the chosen style's way: the path to a layered SVG written from a description (back to front, flat colours, at the frame's shape; see the README, A scene from words). Any style but motif.

medium.about: for the style "motif": what it is drawn with (chalk draws on a dark board)

engines.title: Reanimate engine: vector drawings and maths animations (own engine ported from Reanimate)
engines.about: Self-drawing lines, TeX, colour maps, 20 map projections, Fourier circles, shape morphs and two films; 16:9, 9:16, 1:1, 4:5.

example.about: a ported Reanimate example (its length sets the film's length)

screen.about: the canvas in units; [16, 9] (Reanimate's) fits a 16:9 frame only; left out, the short side is 9 units, so a 1080x1920 reel gets [9, 16]; a value must have the frame's proportions

fit.about: for a reel (9:16, 1:1, 4:5): 'contain' shows a 16:9 example whole with empty bands, 'cover' fills the frame and crops the sides, 'none' keeps unit sizes (the middle of the drawing)
